description: An ultra fast cross-platform multiple screenshots module in pure Python using ctypes.

summary.one_liner: MSS is a pure-Python, dependency-free screenshot library that uses ctypes to capture one or all monitors quickly on Windows, macOS and GNU/Linux.
summary.what_it_does: The library grabs a screenshot of a single monitor or of all monitors combined and can save it to a PNG file. It is written in pure Python using ctypes, so it has no third-party dependencies. The README says it is thread-safe and PEP8 compliant, and requires Python 3.10+. Captured images can be handed to PIL for other formats, or integrated with NumPy and OpenCV. The README says it is suited to embedding in games or computer vision and AI software that need fast, platform-optimized screen capture. Examples and fuller documentation are referenced but not reproduced in the README.
use_cases: capture screenshots of one or all monitors from Python
grab screen frames for computer vision or AI pipelines
feed screen captures into NumPy or OpenCV
save screenshots to PNG files from a script
embed fast screen capture in a game or desktop application
notable: No third-party dependencies; implemented in pure Python with ctypes
Thread-safe screen capture across one or all monitors
Optional integration with PIL, NumPy and OpenCV
caveats: Basic by design: it grabs screenshots and saves PNG, with other formats requiring PIL
On external monitors with scaling/high-DPI issues, some packages call SetProcessDpiAware on import, so mss must be imported first
